title: Iblis asks for time
hook: Iblis refuses again and asks for respite to mislead, except the sincere (38:71–83)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ayyub's spring, cool water after years of illness. Your line was patient; a spring came.

Adam made from clay, the angels told to bow, and one who refused. Iblis, saying I'm better than him: You made me from fire and him from clay. This path met the scene back on day twenty-four, and the lesson was pride. Surah Sad tells it again, and lets it run a few lines further, past the refusal, into a negotiation. Iblis, expelled, doesn't beg to come back. He asks for something else. Time. And in his own boast, he admits there's someone he can't touch.

Verses seventy-one to seventy-six give the refusal: I am better than him. Then seventy-seven and seventy-eight: go out from here, you are rejected, and My curse is on you until the Day of Judgment. Verse seventy-nine. Iblis says: my Lord, then give me respite until the day they are raised. Notice two things. He still says my Lord; he doesn't deny Allah exists, he refuses Him. And he doesn't ask for forgiveness. He asks for time, to use against the people he refused to bow to. Allah answers: you are of those given respite, until the day of the known time. Then the boast, verses eighty-two and eighty-three. He swears by Allah's own might that he'll mislead every one of them, and then he adds the exception himself. Pickthall: "Save Thy single-minded slaves among them." The Arabic is al-mukhlasin, those made sincere, purified. The word is recited two ways in the established readings of the Qur'an: mukhlasin, those Allah has made sincere, and mukhlisin, those who make their worship sincere. Some scholars hold both meanings at once: sincerity is something a person works at, and something given. Either way, the enemy names his own limit. He can whisper to anyone. He can't take someone whose devotion is single-minded, done for Allah alone, not for an audience. The surah closes soon after with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told to say: I ask no payment for this, and I'm not one who pretends. Sincerity, at the start and at the end.

Choose one small thing you'll do today, a kindness, a task, a prayer if you pray, and look at the reason you're doing it. If part of it is for someone to notice, gently set that part down. Imagine doing it with no one ever knowing, only God, or only you, and see whether it feels lighter or harder.
Al-mukhlasin, those made sincere, the one group Iblis admits, in his own boast, that he can never mislead. Today's word.
Your line: the sincere are protected. Even Iblis, in his own boast, names that limit. Rest well.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of ikhlas, sincerity, as doing every act for Allah alone, and many renew their intention (niyya) before prayer, charity and other good deeds.

chat.says: Is there anyone Iblis admits he can't mislead?
options: Yes, in Surah Sad he excepts the sincere, whose devotion is for Allah alone.
Yes, only people who have never made a single mistake in their lives.
No, in his boast he swears to mislead everyone, with no exceptions.
